jobs.title: Director, Google Gemini Enterprise, Data & AI
jobs.description:
Job Description

Toast is recruiting on behalf of one of the world's largest professional services firms, with thousands of people across Canada advising organizations on audit, tax, and advisory work. Their Data & AI practice is one of the fastest growing parts of the firm, driven by strong demand from clients across sectors who want to modernize their data platforms and put AI to work at scale. They are looking for a Director to lead the growth and delivery of Google Gemini Enterprise solutions, owning client engagements from AI strategy through to enterprise-wide implementation while working closely with Google Cloud to build and take joint offerings to market.

Responsibilities

Act as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders, including CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and CFOs, guiding their AI transformation agendas
Lead AI strategy engagements, including maturity assessments, Gemini Enterprise roadmaps, and operating model and governance design
Translate complex business challenges into clear AI-enabled opportunities and value cases
Architect end-to-end Gemini Enterprise solutions covering data integration and grounding, agentic workflows, and security and compliance frameworks
Provide technical oversight across data, AI/ML, and cloud engineering teams to keep delivery cohesive
Advise on scalable deployment models and enterprise integration with ERP, CRM, and collaboration platforms
Lead large-scale AI programs from pilot through enterprise rollout, owning quality, timelines, and value realization
Build reusable assets and accelerators, such as use cases, reference architectures, and deployment playbooks, to scale delivery
Build and manage strategic relationships with Google Cloud, aligning client needs with product roadmap evolution
Co-develop joint solutions and go-to-market offerings with partners and contribute to capability development
Support business development and complex pursuits, including solution shaping, proposals, and pricing models
Present Gemini Enterprise solutions to executive audiences, turning technical concepts into clear business narratives
Drive client-facing storytelling on agentic AI, productivity gains, and ROI
Contribute to thought leadership and market positioning in AI transformation

Requirements

10+ years in consulting, technology, or AI/data leadership roles
Proven track record delivering enterprise AI or cloud transformation programs
Expertise in enterprise AI architecture and design
Strong expertise in generative AI and LLMs, enterprise data architecture, and cloud platforms, with experience on GCP considered an asset
Experience engaging and influencing C-suite stakeholders
Ability to shape, position, and close complex deals
Demonstrated success contributing to business development and revenue growth
Experience with the Google Cloud ecosystem and strategic alliances
Exposure to AI agents, agentic workflows, and enterprise AI governance frameworks
Track record building repeatable consulting offerings and intellectual property

Benefits

Compensation listed on the posting is for base salary only. Total salary includes base salary + annual bonuses.
Comprehensive Total Rewards program
Lead a flagship Google Gemini Enterprise practice inside one of the fastest growing teams at the firm
Shape how major Canadian organizations across sectors adopt generative and agentic AI, moving them from pilot projects to enterprise-wide rollouts
Work directly with Google Cloud to influence product roadmaps and build joint offerings that reach clients across the country
Build the playbooks, reference architectures, and IP that will define how the firm delivers AI transformation for years to come
Application Review

Submit your application, including your resume and cover letter, through our online portal. Our team will carefully review your qualifications and experiences. We take pride in responding promptly, so if your application aligns with our current opportunities, you’ll hear back from us with next steps. Your journey with Toast begins here, and we’re excited to see what you bring to the table!

Vetting Call

If your application is successful, we’ll schedule a vetting call with a member of the Toast team. This 30-45 minute informal conversation is designed for us to get to know you better and assess your skills. Be prepared to discuss your past projects, the challenges you’ve tackled, and the impact you’ve made. This is your chance to shine and show us why you’re a great fit for the roles we offer.

Profile Creation

Once you’ve impressed us in the vetting call, we’ll create an unbiased profile that highlights your experience while minimizing common biases. Instead, we focus on your skills, industry experience, and the impact you’ve made. This way, your profile reflects your true potential and accomplishments.

Client Submission

After crafting your unbiased profile, we submit it to our trusted clients. We work closely with these clients to ensure they understand the value you bring. Throughout their interview process, we remain by your side, providing support and guidance. Our goal is to help you navigate the hiring process smoothly and confidently, ensuring you have the best chance to secure a role that fits your skills and aspirations.

jobs.title: Director, Workplace Strategy
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You’ll Be Doing

As a member of the Enterprise Real Estate and Workplace Experience team, you’ll help shape a modern, connected, inclusive, and high-performing workplace experience across CIBC’s real estate portfolio, including flagship and enterprise environments. As a Director, Workplace Strategy, you’ll lead the evolution, translation, and implementation of CIBC’s Global Workplace Experience Strategy across workplace transformation projects. You’ll provide strategic advice, develop workplace standards and enablement approaches, and use research, data, and team member feedback to help reimagine how we work. You’ll partner with leaders across Real Estate, Human Resources, Design, Technology, and other key functions to align workplace strategy with business priorities, future workforce needs, and enterprise transformation goals. You’ll also prepare clear recommendations and insights for senior leaders to support decision-making and the delivery of CIBC’s future workplace strategy.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote. Details on your work arrangement will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How You’ll Succeed

Lead workplace strategy execution – Translate CIBC’s Global Workplace Experience Strategy into practical design strategies, standards and enablement approaches for real estate transformation projects across the portfolio.
Provide strategic advice – Partner with leaders and project teams to apply workplace experience principles, align initiatives to enterprise priorities, and recommend solutions that improve the workplace experience and support the future of work.
Use insights to inform decisions – Conduct market research, evaluate internal and external trends, and use employee feedback and workplace data to identify opportunities, inform recommendations, and strengthen strategic planning.
Support change and enablement – Develop materials, approaches, and change tactics that help leaders and team members adapt to evolving workplace environments and new ways of working.
Build strong partnerships – Work closely with partners across Enterprise Real Estate, Human Resources, Design, Technology, Corporate Security, Events, Retail, and Facilities Management to support coordinated planning and successful implementation.
Present to senior leadership – Prepare clear, compelling findings, business cases, and recommendations for senior leaders and executive forums, highlighting benefits, risks, dependencies, and considerations for decision-making.

Who You Are

You can demonstrate 10 years of experience in workplace strategy, strategic planning and real estate transformation, and change enablement. You have experience in workplace design, employee experience, operating model change, or enterprise transformation in a large, complex organization.
You have a degree or diploma in a relevant field. It’s an asset if you have education or experience related to workplace strategy, business strategy, design, organizational change, or real estate.
You’re future focused. You look beyond the moment and help shape strategies that will make a difference today and tomorrow. You identify opportunities to evolve the workplace in support of business and workforce priorities.
You’re analytical. You give meaning to data and research. You enjoy investigating complicated problems, identifying trends, and turning insights into clear, practical recommendations. You have well-developed communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal.
You’re influential. Your influence makes a difference. You build credibility with senior leaders and partners and help bring about change by sharing your expertise and recommendations in a clear and thoughtful way.
You’re collaborative. You’re motivated by collective success and work effectively across functions to bring people together, align priorities, and deliver shared outcomes.
You’re a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing strategic team goals, creating clarity around priorities and ways of working, and coaching others to support strong performance and growth.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

careers@ontariohealth.ca
. Requests will be addressed within three business days, and the application window will be extended by three business days.

At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care. 

What Ontario Health offers:  

Role

At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:

Comprehensive health coverage from day one, with fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits to support you and your family’s health
Flexible health care or wellness spending accounts, plus an inclusive program to support your overall well-being
A premium defined benefit pension plan, ensuring long-term financial security
Competitive vacation entitlement that encourages time to rest and recharge
Three personal days and two float days annually, providing added flexibility to support work-life balance, in addition to vacation days
Ongoing learning and career development opportunities designed to help you grow, advance, and thrive in your profession
A collaborative, values-driven workplace where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team

Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity. 

As Director, Planning and Implementation, you will lead health system strategies that respond to regional needs and advance integrated, equitable care. Reporting to the Vice President, System Strategy, Planning, Design and Implementation, you will turn strategic priorities into achievable program plans and oversee their implementation and evaluation.

Lead a cross-functional team and collaborate with regional and provincial partners across health sectors to close system gaps, strengthen coordination and deliver results. You will be accountable for your portfolio’s planning, team performance, and day-to-day program operations.

This regional role supports the health care needs and priorities of the North East Region.

Here Is What You Will Be Doing

Drive regional strategy: Assess health care needs, set priorities and lead integrated planning, implementation and evaluation aligned with provincial and regional strategies and Ontario Health’s Strategic Plan and Annual Business Plan.
Turn evidence into action: Work with regional colleagues to identify data sources and analysis that inform decisions, strengthen planning, and improve performance. Embed health equity principles and priorities throughout planning processes.
Build partnerships across sectors: Establish committees and communities of practice, engage internal and external partners, and connect regional and provincial teams to address system barriers, resource needs and accountability gaps.
Advance integration and innovation: Represent the portfolio on regional committees and other collaborative bodies, champion best practices and integrated care models, and recommend program improvements and funding allocation priorities informed by emerging health system issues.
Lead people and operations: Guide and manage staff, oversee day-to-day program operations, and ensure work follows accepted best practices, government and ministry directives, and regional policies and procedures.
Deliver measurable results: Establish regional goals and implement initiatives to achieve them. Monitor, evaluate, and report on activities against performance objectives set by the CRO.

Education And Experience

Here is what you will need to be successful:

Master’s degree in health or business administration, or equivalent education/experience.
7 years of work experience in the public or private health care sector.
5 years of experience leading or managing teams directly or indirectly, using relationship-building and management skills, with a solid background in managing staff to achieve corporate objectives.
Solid background in integrating large, complex initiatives in a changing environment, with advanced project management skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects.

Knowledge And Skills

Business acumen: Apply business principles and systems thinking in health care, including financial and human resource management, organizational dynamics and governance, strategic planning, risk management and quality improvement.
Stakeholder engagement and relationship management: Develop networks, alliances and multiple external collaborative relationships that support department performance. Collaborate across functions and boundaries, find common ground with an expanding range of stakeholders, identify key issues, and accommodate key players’ needs on joint projects with external parties or units.
Communication and interpersonal skills: Highly developed verbal and written communication skills to provide and obtain complex, technical or sensitive information effectively, clearly, concisely and logically, at an appropriate level and in an appropriate format. Prepare and deliver presentations on technical and/or sensitive information to diverse audiences. Listen well, encourage open communication, and respond appropriately to others’ needs, feelings and capabilities with tact, compassion, sensitivity, and respect.
Judgement and negotiation: Exercise sound judgement on sensitive and contentious issues and negotiate consensus on complex policy strategies.
Strategic planning and risk management: Align department tasks and objectives with corporate goals, establish clear targets and measures to track progress, evaluate outcomes and adjust direction as appropriate.
Change management: Actively embrace change initiatives to improve department performance and use varied methods to help employees respond positively to change.
Health care planning and system design: Expert knowledge of planning models and approaches, with an understanding of the health care system and environment. Scan for ideas, best practices and system-wide trends, and effectively select options, plan, implement and evaluate health care policies and/or programs.
Program development and innovation: Develop new insights and apply innovative solutions to improve the organization. Foster creative thinking and innovation, and design and implement new or cutting-edge programs and processes.
Health sector and community knowledge: Knowledge of Ontario’s health sector and workforce trends; in-depth knowledge of local health issues, priorities and needs in the context of broader health care policy and system development trends; and knowledge of the needs of Indigenous peoples in urban and community settings and Francophone communities.

jobs.title: VP Technology and Innovation Partners
jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

Dayforce is the AI-powered people platform. One platform for HR, Pay, Time, Talent, and Analytics, with AI built into how work gets done. Partners are central to that strategy. The AI capabilities, data, and solutions our partners bring to the platform extend what Dayforce AI can do for customers and accelerate how fast we grow.

That is changing what our technology ecosystem does for the business. Partners are moving from integrations that sit next to the platform to AI-enabled solutions we resell, transact, and build on together. That shift touches revenue, product strategy, and how Dayforce competes.

The VP, Technology and Innovation Partners owns the strategy, performance, and commercial outcomes of Dayforce’s technology partner ecosystem across five areas: ISV partners Dayforce resells, including Go1, Emburse, Docusign, Aquera, etc.; ISV partners with certified connectors on the Dayforce Exchange across Pay and Benefits and HR and Talent; the Microsoft partnership; In Country Payroll partners; and Dayforce Build.

This is a leader-of-leaders role with a number attached. You will be accountable for resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, marketplace revenue, and the quality of the integrations and solutions partners deliver. You will lead an established team of four senior leaders who own the Microsoft alliance, In Country Payroll, Pay and Benefits ISVs, and HR and Talent ISVs. You will operate as a peer to the leaders of our Services Delivery and Community pillars. We are looking for a leader with the commercial, go-to-market, and technology depth to run all of it as one business.

Work is what you do, not where you go. For this role, we are open to remote work and can hire anywhere in the US or Canada.

What You’ll Get To Do

Business Ownership and Growth

Carry the technology partner number. Own resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, and marketplace revenue, with clear accountability to the CRO organization.
Scale software resell. Grow attach of resold partner solutions to core Dayforce deals. Set the margins, pricing, packaging, and commercial terms that make resell a material, predictable revenue line.
Make the Exchange transactable. Share ownership with Product of moving the Dayforce Exchange from referral-only to transactable. Own the partner commercial model, partner onboarding, and partner readiness.
Make partners a growth engine for Dayforce AI. Build the partner strategy that extends the AI-powered people platform. Bring in the AI partners, agents, and solutions that deepen what Dayforce AI delivers for customers and create new revenue.
Own the portfolio. Decide which partners we resell, which we integrate and refer, which we co-build with, and which we retire. Close gaps in the Dayforce offering through build, partner, or buy recommendations with Product and Corporate Development.

Microsoft

Serve as executive sponsor for Microsoft, supporting the alliance lead who owns the day-to-day relationship across partnership, sales, and product teams.
Grow Dayforce’s position as a strategic HCM and payroll partner in the Microsoft ecosystem, across Azure, Dynamics 365, Copilot, and Teams.
Build and run a joint HCM, Pay, and ERP go-to-market with Microsoft and the SI partners that deliver it, including marketplace, co-sell programs, and field-to-field engagement.
Lead AI co-innovation that turns Microsoft technology into differentiated Dayforce AI capability.

Global Payroll and In-Country Partners

Own the strategy and performance of the In Country Payroll network that delivers and extends Dayforce global payroll.
Set standards for coverage, service quality, compliance, integration, and customer experience, and hold partners to them.
Rationalize and expand country coverage based on customer demand and deal pipeline.
Work with Product and Operations to deliver one consistent global payroll experience, whether Dayforce or a partner runs the payroll.

Dayforce Build

Dayforce Build is the platform customers and partners use to build integrations, extensions, and new capabilities on Dayforce. Partners are already building in it. This role turns that early momentum into a scaled partner ecosystem.

Own the partner strategy and growth of Dayforce Build, sharing ownership of the platform roadmap with Product and Engineering.
Move partner builds, including AI-powered extensions and agents, from proof of concept to production, certified, and in market.
Recruit and grow the ISVs, SIs, and developers building on the platform, including through the Dayforce Developer Community.
Connect what partners build to the Exchange, the resell program, and field go-to-market so builds turn into revenue.
Set quality, security, and certification standards for everything partners build on Dayforce.

GTM and Field Execution

Build repeatable joint go-to-market motions with priority partners: co-sell plays, joint campaigns, enablement, and account mapping.
Drive field adoption of resell and partner solutions across segments.
Equip Dayforce sellers with the positioning, pricing, and proof points to attach partner solutions to core deals, so partner attach is a default consideration rather than an exception.
Partner with Marketing on ecosystem launches, events, and partner showcases.

Leading the Team

You will lead four senior leaders, each running a distinct motion. Your first job is to make them operate as one ecosystem.

Microsoft Alliance owns the day-to-day Microsoft relationship, co-sell, and joint GTM.
In Country Payroll owns the global payroll partner network, coverage, and service quality.
Pay and Benefits ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce Pay and Benefits through connectors and resell.
HR and Talent ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce HR and Talent through connectors and resell.
Coach, develop, and raise the bar across the team. Have a clear point of view on strengths and gaps within your first quarter.
Establish one scorecard and operating rhythm across all five areas, balancing long-term platform strategy against near-term revenue.

Technology and Product Influence

Serve as the technical voice of the partner ecosystem inside Dayforce.
Partner with Product and Engineering on integration architecture, APIs, connector certification, and partner developer experience.
Partner with Product on the Dayforce AI roadmap, so partner AI capabilities complement and extend what Dayforce builds.
Scout emerging technology and AI partners that expand the Dayforce platform and create new revenue.

Executive and Cross-Functional Influence

Operate as a trusted counterpart to executive leadership across Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and Finance.
Negotiate complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements, and hold partners accountable through data, not sentiment.
Present performance, risk, and opportunity directly to the executive team with clarity and conviction, including in forums with sponsor visibility.
Executive exposure to the CRO, Product, and Technology organizations, and to Microsoft executive leadership, as a matter of routine, not exception.

Skills And Experience We Value

15+ years in enterprise software, with at least 7 years leading technology partnerships, alliances, or ecosystem businesses, and meaningful time spent carrying a number.
A track record of growing partner revenue, including resell or OEM models, with specifics: bookings delivered, attach rates moved, marketplace revenue grown.
Direct experience scaling a SaaS marketplace, app ecosystem, or developer platform program, ideally including the move to a transactable model.
Deep experience with Microsoft or another hyperscaler: co-sell programs, marketplace, and executive sponsorship.
Strong commercial judgment. You have structured and negotiated complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements.
Enough technical depth to lead conversations on APIs, integration architecture, cloud platforms, and AI with engineering teams on both sides.
A clear point of view on how AI is reshaping software ecosystems, and experience bringing AI partners and solutions to market.
Experience leading senior leaders who each run a distinct business and making them operate as one team.
Familiarity with HCM, payroll, ERP, or an adjacent enterprise platform category.
Comfort operating in a private equity-backed environment, with the pace, transparency, and accountability that entails.
Highly analytical and metrics-driven, at ease in complex matrixed environments and in front of an executive audience.

What Would Make You Stand Out

Global payroll experience is a strong advantage.
Prior PE-backed experience is a strong advantage.

What’s In It For You

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Dayforce encourages personal and professional growth. We offer excellent time away from work programs, comprehensive wellness initiatives and recognition through competitive pay and benefits.

With a commitment to community impact, including volunteer days and our charity, Dayforce Cares we provide opportunities for you to thrive both in your career and personal life. Our focus is not just on your job but on supporting you to be the best version of yourself.

This job posting is for an existing vacancy

Artificial intelligence may be used in the screening, assessment, or selection of applicants for this position.

Dayforce is committed to providing accommodations for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please contact us at accessibilty@dayforce.com.

The final compensation offered may vary based on a variety of factors, including bonuses and/or incentives, or a candidate’s experience, skills, budget and location. Our company is committed to providing a fair, equitable, and competitive package that reflects the value an individual brings to the organization.

Further, our back office support teams, including but not limited to Human Resources, are primarily English speaking. jobs.description:
About Clutch

We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars. Are you game?

Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee… and that’s just the beginning. Named to The Globe and Mail’s list of Canada’s Top Growing Companies for six consecutive years and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50™ and Fast 500™ lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team. Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Altos Ventures, BMO Capital Partners, Canaan, Real Ventures, and others. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.

Finance at Clutch

We’re growing rapidly, with in‑house re‑conditioning centres, a captive lending platform and a national logistics network, we combine manufacturing‑grade operations with tech‑enabled consumer experience. We plan to be public company ready within 24–36 months and are building the finance foundation to get there. Strong systems keep our numbers accurate, our close on time, and financial information flowing clearly across the company, and they give leadership the confidence to make bold, well-timed decisions.

About The Role

Clutch is looking for a Director, Financial Reporting to step in as a critical leader on our finance team. Reporting directly to the Corporate Controller, you will architect the framework that turns thousands of data points per vehicle into clean, decision‑grade financial reporting. You will take charge of IFRS compliance, external audit readiness, and the design and implementation of a strong internal controls environment ahead of IPO readiness. You will lead a growing team that loves the craft of accounting as much as you do, taking ownership of the reporting cycle and technical accounting while partnering with Financial Systems leadership to drive ERP evolution.

What You’ll Do

Build and run the monthly, quarterly, and annual close; deliver accurate financial statements and supplementary financial information on tight deadlines.
Design and implement internal‑control, risk‑management, and policy frameworks to achieve NI 52‑109 readiness.
Lead external audits and statutory reporting; manage relationships with auditors and regulators.
Drive ERP/finance‑stack evolution in partnership with Financial Systems leadership
Build, mentor, and scale an accounting/reporting team; set clear performance standards and foster a culture of ownership and precision.
Build and leverage automations and AI to improve efficiency, reduce cost and risk.
Own cost and inventory accounting to support accurate financial statements.

What We’re Looking For

CPA with 8-10+ years’ progressive accounting leadership
Big 4 experience required; subsequent industry experience is considered an asset but is not mandatory
Command of IFRS plus advanced knowledge of revenue recognition, manufacturing, leasing, consolidation, and complex equity / debt transactions.
Proven experience establishing and strengthening internal control frameworks and implementing modern ERP and financial systems; experience with Oracle Fusion is considered an asset.
Experience building and leading teams, with a relentless attention to detail, ownership mentality, and a passion for building processes from the ground up.
Deep manufacturing or complex supply‑chain experience: cost accounting, inventory valuation, production labor, and overhead allocation are second nature.
Superb communicator able to translate accounting insights to non‑finance partners.

Why You'll Love It At Clutch

Be part of a disruptive, tech-driven company that is transforming the automotive industry — one of the largest and fastest-growing B2C startups in Canada.
A unique opportunity to work at the center of the company, helping shape how Clutch communicates, operates, and executes as we scale.
Freedom to innovate and ownership of your role — work on meaningful and challenging projects that have a direct impact on the business.
Collaborate with a talented and passionate team in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
Competitive pay and equity incentives.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Opportunities for growth and development in a rapidly scaling company.

Benefits: Comprehensive healthcare, dental, vision, prescriptions, life insurance, and dependent coverage; starting from day 1.

Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer-focused solutions.

Operating through our family of brands – CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud – our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services. Learn more at: https://nestogroup.ca/

Work Location

Hybrid, based in our Toronto or Montreal office. In-office expectations vary with business needs. If you are based in Montreal, expect to travel to Toronto a couple of times per month.

Why We Are Hiring

Maestro, our AI-powered underwriting platform, already runs inside nesto, with AI agents making real-time, policy-based decisions. We are now bringing it to financial institution clients through Nesto Cloud. You will be the first leader of client AI delivery. Your mission is to run the program that puts a fleet of AI agents live in Canadian banks’ production environments. As our Director of AI Delivery, you'll own it end to end: the delivery plan, the pod, the day-to-day client relationship, and the evidence that moves each agent through requirements, testing, model-risk approval, live-file shadow, joint change management, and progressive production activation. You will also write the repeatable deployment playbook we reuse for every client that follows.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead Maestro delivery. Set a clear delivery approach amid uncertainty and build trust with client executives.
Own the plan and stage exits. Own the plan across underwriting agents. Call each stage exit against its written proof point across our 9 stages: scoping, process mapping, golden sets, configuration, evaluation, model governance, shadow, change management, and progressive production decisioning.
Lead the pod. Lead a senior delivery pod (delivery managers, underwriting expert, data scientists, program PM) day to day. Guide the AI Delivery Managers as they gather requirements for each agent. Work with the assigned PM and the relevant delivery and technical colleagues to keep implementations moving. Run standups and working sessions, and build and defend the steering narrative. The client Sponsor makes the final call on the story.
Chair eval review. Run the weekly review of agent performance evidence and turn it into build and tuning priorities for Engineering. Data Scientists produce the evidence. You review it and do not produce it yourself.
Lead the model-risk relationship. Lead the relationship with the client’s model-risk team. Land validation packages for each condition family and secure the risk and governance sign-offs that authorize shadow and production.
Run the shadow program. Adjudicate divergences, re-validate for drift, and report value foregone to client executives each month.
Own change management and readiness. Co-own the joint readiness sign-off with the client and make sure the pilot group is trained and running the new workflow.
Build the deployment playbook. Write the repeatable process that takes AI agents from client requirements through testing and client approval into production. Document each agent’s deployment as you go. The playbook is a core deliverable, not a retrospective.
Protect scope. Hold client “small asks” to the config log and SOW change process. Nothing gets absorbed silently.

What You Bring

You have a client-facing delivery background, as an engagement manager, Delivery Director, or Implementation Director.
You have run senior delivery teams on client sites and led working sessions with EVP-level executives.
You have led client AI implementations hands-on, from requirements through production.
You know ML/AI delivery well enough to chair an eval review, question precision and recall trade-offs, and translate model evidence into language a risk committee can act on.
You define written exit criteria, produce the artifacts that back them, and document decisions.

Nice-to-Have

Experience implementing AI for banks or other regulated organizations, including model-risk validation.
Experience implementing your own company’s product at the client.
Mortgage or retail-credit domain knowledge, or experience with staged production rollouts of decisioning systems.
Comfort building the playbook while running it in a scale-up.

This Role Might Be for You If

You have delivered AI solutions for enterprise clients on high-visibility projects and know how to earn their stakeholders’ trust.
You get energized when there is no playbook to follow and can turn uncertainty into a clear, structured approach.
You do well under high expectations on a project that matters deeply to the client.
You work well with a growing team of delivery, product, and technical colleagues.

Interview Process

Recruiter Screen (30 min): A quick intro call to learn about your background and give you a real picture of the role.
Discovery Call (30 min): A conversation with the hiring manager to dig into your experience and assess mutual fit.
Case Study: A chance to showcase your skills through an open-ended, scenario-based exercise relevant to the role.
Case Study Interview (60 min): A deep dive into your submission, with time to get to know some team members and ask about the role and company.
Final Non-Technical Interview (60 min): You'll meet with the recruiter and two additional stakeholders for a final conversation before a decision is made.
Offer Stage: Pending successful background and role-specific vetting checks, you'll receive a formal offer to join the team.

Why You'll Love Working Here

We believe great people do their best work when they're supported professionally, personally, and financially. That's why we offer a comprehensive rewards package designed to help you thrive at every stage of your career.

Competitive Rewards – Competitive compensation, performance incentives (where applicable), and recognition for your contributions.

Family Support – Enhanced maternity and parental leave top-up programs.
Learning & Growth – Education assistance, mentorship, training, and opportunities to build your career across Nesto Group.
Tools for Success – Modern technology, collaborative teams, and the resources you need to do your best work.

Life at nesto

At nesto, we're passionate about challenging the status quo and building a better mortgage experience and saving money on their mortgages for Canadians. We foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, and creativity where every team member is empowered to take ownership, make an impact, and grow. If you're looking to solve meaningful problems alongside ambitious, supportive teammates, you'll feel right at home here.

The bright side of mortgages

nesto is Canada's leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go – with total transparency and no haggling.

About Us

As Canada's pioneer in online mortgage lending, nesto is transforming the way Canadians finance their homes. Our mission is to offer a positive, empowering, and transparent property financing experience, simplified from start to finish.

Borrowers benefit from rates that are often lower than those offered by the big banks, along with an exceptional end-to-end mortgage experience powered by best-in-class AI technology. Fast, simple, and fully digital, nesto has been recognized as CLA Lender of the Year for three consecutive years. That's the bright side of mortgages.

Nesto Group

Nesto Group is Canada's leading provider of mortgage technology and financing solutions, with more than CAD $80 billion in residential and commercial mortgages under administration. Trusted by many of the country's leading financial institutions, we combine over 50 years of mortgage expertise with proprietary cloud and AI technology to transform the future of lending.

Powered by our proprietary cloud and AI technology, nesto has become one of Canada's fastest-growing mortgage lenders, gaining market share across direct-to-consumer (D2C) residential lending, the broker channel, and multi-family commercial lending. Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer-focused solutions.

Operating through our family of brands – CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud – our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services. Learn more at: https://nestogroup.ca/

Work Location

Hybrid, based in our Toronto or Montreal office. In-office expectations vary with business needs. If you are based in Montreal, expect to travel to Toronto a couple of times per month.

Why We Are Hiring

Maestro, our AI-powered underwriting platform, already runs inside nesto, with AI agents making real-time, policy-based decisions. We are now bringing it to financial institution clients through Nesto Cloud. You will be the first leader of client AI delivery. Your mission is to run the program that puts a fleet of AI agents live in Canadian banks’ production environments. As our Director of AI Delivery, you'll own it end to end: the delivery plan, the pod, the day-to-day client relationship, and the evidence that moves each agent through requirements, testing, model-risk approval, live-file shadow, joint change management, and progressive production activation. You will also write the repeatable deployment playbook we reuse for every client that follows.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead Maestro delivery. Set a clear delivery approach amid uncertainty and build trust with client executives.
Own the plan and stage exits. Own the plan across underwriting agents. Call each stage exit against its written proof point across our 9 stages: scoping, process mapping, golden sets, configuration, evaluation, model governance, shadow, change management, and progressive production decisioning.
Lead the pod. Lead a senior delivery pod (delivery managers, underwriting expert, data scientists, program PM) day to day. Guide the AI Delivery Managers as they gather requirements for each agent. Work with the assigned PM and the relevant delivery and technical colleagues to keep implementations moving. Run standups and working sessions, and build and defend the steering narrative. The client Sponsor makes the final call on the story.
Chair eval review. Run the weekly review of agent performance evidence and turn it into build and tuning priorities for Engineering. Data Scientists produce the evidence. You review it and do not produce it yourself.
Lead the model-risk relationship. Lead the relationship with the client’s model-risk team. Land validation packages for each condition family and secure the risk and governance sign-offs that authorize shadow and production.
Run the shadow program. Adjudicate divergences, re-validate for drift, and report value foregone to client executives each month.
Own change management and readiness. Co-own the joint readiness sign-off with the client and make sure the pilot group is trained and running the new workflow.
Build the deployment playbook. Write the repeatable process that takes AI agents from client requirements through testing and client approval into production. Document each agent’s deployment as you go. The playbook is a core deliverable, not a retrospective.
Protect scope. Hold client “small asks” to the config log and SOW change process. Nothing gets absorbed silently.

What You Bring

You have a client-facing delivery background, as an engagement manager, Delivery Director, or Implementation Director.
You have run senior delivery teams on client sites and led working sessions with EVP-level executives.
You have led client AI implementations hands-on, from requirements through production.
You know ML/AI delivery well enough to chair an eval review, question precision and recall trade-offs, and translate model evidence into language a risk committee can act on.
You define written exit criteria, produce the artifacts that back them, and document decisions.

Nice-to-Have

Experience implementing AI for banks or other regulated organizations, including model-risk validation.
Experience implementing your own company’s product at the client.
Mortgage or retail-credit domain knowledge, or experience with staged production rollouts of decisioning systems.
Comfort building the playbook while running it in a scale-up.

This Role Might Be for You If

You have delivered AI solutions for enterprise clients on high-visibility projects and know how to earn their stakeholders’ trust.
You get energized when there is no playbook to follow and can turn uncertainty into a clear, structured approach.
You do well under high expectations on a project that matters deeply to the client.
You work well with a growing team of delivery, product, and technical colleagues.

Interview Process

Recruiter Screen (30 min): A quick intro call to learn about your background and give you a real picture of the role.
Discovery Call (30 min): A conversation with the hiring manager to dig into your experience and assess mutual fit.
Case Study: A chance to showcase your skills through an open-ended, scenario-based exercise relevant to the role.
Case Study Interview (60 min): A deep dive into your submission, with time to get to know some team members and ask about the role and company.
Final Non-Technical Interview (60 min): You'll meet with the recruiter and two additional stakeholders for a final conversation before a decision is made.
Offer Stage: Pending successful background and role-specific vetting checks, you'll receive a formal offer to join the team.

Why You'll Love Working Here

We believe great people do their best work when they're supported professionally, personally, and financially. That's why we offer a comprehensive rewards package designed to help you thrive at every stage of your career.

Competitive Rewards – Competitive compensation, performance incentives (where applicable), and recognition for your contributions.
Health & Wellness – Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, Health & Wellness Spending Accounts (where applicable), telemedicine, Employee Assistance Programs, and mental health support for you and your family.
Time to Recharge – Generous vacation (4 weeks), floater days, and statutory holidays to help you recharge.
Planning for the Future – RRSP matching to support your long-term financial wellbeing.
Family Support – Enhanced maternity and parental leave top-up programs.
Learning & Growth – Education assistance, mentorship, training, and opportunities to build your career across Nesto Group.
Tools for Success – Modern technology, collaborative teams, and the resources you need to do your best work.

Life at nesto

At nesto, we're passionate about challenging the status quo and building a better mortgage experience and saving money on their mortgages for Canadians. We foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, and creativity where every team member is empowered to take ownership, make an impact, and grow. If you're looking to solve meaningful problems alongside ambitious, supportive teammates, you'll feel right at home here.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At Nesto Group, we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to succeed.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis), persons with disabilities, members of racialized communities, women, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

If you require accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process, we are committed to working with you to meet your needs.
